sermon.title: Has the U.S. Government Made Just Choices and Equal Choices?
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Has the U.S. Government Made Just Choices and Equal Choices?”, Pastor David G. Kincer reads the Declaration of Independence and the Preamble of the Constitution and says government is to protect moral rights and promote, not provide, the general welfare. He teaches that the Bible’s purposes include moving us from bad government to good, equal rights for all peoples in Christ, and a just judicial system. He then lists unjust and unequal choices past and present and calls government to repent or be replaced.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he reads the Declaration as “certain unchangeable rights” (the text says “unalienable”); the captions give “consent of the government,” read here as “governed.” He quotes Colossians 1:13 (“delivered us from the power of darkness”) without naming it. He speaks about women’s rights, American Indians (sterilization, children taken to schools, citizenship in 1924), slavery and hush harbors, the Supreme Court and Darwin, Chinese immigration (1882-1943) and property (1965), censorship of Christians, the Federal Reserve and welfare, all as his own account; these are kept as spoken. His figures (black citizenship in 1870, 5 million children abused a year, 450,000 sexually, 500 a week in the military, 500 a year in schools, $1.1 trillion a year in welfare, three times all wars, an $18 trillion debt, 50 percent in taxes) have not been checked here.

chunks.short_answer: He reads that all men are created equal and endowed by their Creator with rights, and says the Bible Creator is the standard of justice, and rights are the freedom to do moral things: “not the pursuit of crime.”
chunks.text: Okay, we appreciate you joining us in our pursuit of clarity on crucial choices. Today we will address the question: has the United States of America’s government made just and equal choices? And we will start with the Declaration of Independence. We hold these truths to be self-evident. The Declaration of Independence is the purpose for changing a government. “We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal,” then, “they are provided by their Creator,” you notice they refer to the Bible and God, created, Creator, “with certain unchangeable rights.” So the Bible Creator is the standard of just and rights, and rights are the freedom to do moral things. “And among these rights are life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” not the pursuit of crime, not the pursuit of immorality, but the pursuit of happiness. “And to protect these rights, governments are instituted among men, deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed.”

chunks.section_question: How has the U.S. government treated women unjustly?
chunks.short_answer: Citing 1 Peter 2:14 on a just judicial system, he says women in the past could not vote, sit on a jury, own property if married, get higher education, or get their children in a divorce.
chunks.text: Another purpose of the Bible: to choose a just judicial system to protect our rights. First Peter 2:14: governors are for the punishment of evildoers and for the praise of them that do well. And so the Bible tells us to choose a judicial system that will protect the rights of the moral people. Our government’s unjust and unequal choices: in the past, women could not vote, could not be on a jury, could not own property if they were married, they couldn’t get higher education, and they couldn’t get their kids in a divorce.

chunks.short_answer: He says government must admit it is wrong, repent, and enforce constitutional and Bible morality, or be replaced, as the Declaration says the people may alter or abolish it.
chunks.text: leaving only food and clothing and whatever. So the parent, both parents have to work to provide a normal middle-class lifestyle, and thus the children are left alone till the parents get home. We have 1.1 trillion a year federal and state welfare expenditures. Since 1965 we have three times more spent on welfare than all the wars that we’ve been in put together. The federal debt is at 18 trillion and growing. 50 percent is our tax revenue when you add all the taxes. So what is the solution? Government must, government must admit they are wrong. As the Declaration of Independence says, it is the right of the people to alter or to abolish it and to institute a new government.
